messages.content:
Cocaine is a powerful stimulant drug made from the leaves of the coca plant, which is native to South America. It affects the brain by increasing levels of dopamine, a chemical involved in reward, energy, and pleasure.

It has limited medical use as a local anesthetic in some surgeries, but it is more commonly known as an illegal recreational drug. It may appear as a white powder that is snorted, dissolved and injected, or rubbed on gums. A smokable form, often called “crack cocaine,” is especially fast-acting.

Cocaine can cause short-term effects such as euphoria, alertness, increased heart rate, reduced appetite, anxiety, paranoia, and impaired judgment. It can also be highly addictive and can lead to serious harms, including heart attack, stroke, seizures, overdose, and mental health problems—even in people without known heart disease.

If you or someone else may be experiencing chest pain, trouble breathing, severe agitation, seizures, or loss of consciousness after using cocaine, seek emergency medical help immediately.

Cocaine is a powerful stimulant drug made from the leaves of the coca plant, which grows mainly in South America. It is sometimes used medically as a local anesthetic in limited settings, but it is more commonly known as an illegal recreational drug.

It typically appears as a white powder that may be snorted, dissolved and injected, or smoked in a processed form called crack cocaine. Cocaine increases dopamine activity in the brain, which can cause short-lived feelings of energy, confidence, alertness, and euphoria.

It also carries serious risks, including addiction, anxiety, paranoia, heart attack, stroke, seizures, overdose, and death—especially when mixed with alcohol, opioids, or other drugs. Regular use can harm the heart, brain, nose, lungs, and mental health.
